html:
SMTO-EVT-0006 — SMTO couldn't set up this monitor

GUID: 16510ba2-f1e1-4320-a5fd-ad23edceea69
Slug: monitor-request-invalid
Domain: EVT · Subsystem: evt

What happened

  • A monitor (a repeated check SMTO runs on a Gateway) needs a command to run, or a description clear enough to turn into one. This request had neither, or asked for an unknown monitor status. Nothing was created. This usually comes from a script or another tool.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If a script or other tool created this monitor, ask its owner to include the command to run, or a description specific enough for SMTO to write one. A request with no command and no usable description is refused.
  2. If a tool lists monitors by status, have it use only: queued, running, triggered, completed, failed, cancelled, paused, interrupted or archived. Any other status word is refused.
  3. Or, in a conversation, ask SMTO to start a monitor and say what to check, where, how often and for how long, such as "check disk space every minute for an hour". SMTO then writes and starts the monitor itself, so no separate tool is needed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO confirms the monitor was created and shows its status, such as running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the tool you used, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't give the monitor a vague or broad command just to get past this; it runs that command again and again on your computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The monitor API rejected the request: the list status filter is not a supported monitor status (400), or monitor creation still has no command after optional prompt drafting (422).

What this means

  • Monitor listing receives an unsupported status, or monitor creation still has no command after any prompt-drafting step. Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.

Why this can happen

  • Monitor listing receives an unsupported status, or monitor creation still has no command after any prompt-drafting step.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether this is a list-filter error or incomplete creation request before changing monitor settings.

How to fix it

  • For GET /api/agent/monitors use status queued, running, triggered, completed, failed, cancelled, paused, interrupted or archived. For POST /api/agent/monitors supply command, or a prompt the drafter can turn into a complete command (check missing_details from POST /api/agent/monitors/draft), and review the target Gateway, interval and duration before saving.
  • Provide the intended bounded command or prompt and a supported monitor status. Review its target and schedule before saving.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The list uses a supported status, or a complete deliberate command passes monitor creation validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
